script.title: The Tonic Crusader: How Captain Hadacol Became a 1950s Superhero
script.description: A 1951 promotional comic documentary following the heroic Captain Hadacol as he battles thieves and uncovers hidden treasure in Louisiana.

shots.narration: Captain Hadacol is buried alive in a collapsing mine!
It all starts with a mysterious treasure map.
John and his friends struggle to find the starting point.
They hide the map in a desk drawer for safety.
But thieves are watching from the shadows.
A noise wakes John as the map is stolen.
He reaches for his bottle of Hadacol.
One sip transforms him into the mighty Captain Hadacol.
He quickly dispatches the thief with his super strength.
But the crooks escape with the map overnight.
Red and his sister spot a broken horseshoe on the trail.
They secretly follow the gang into the desert.
A loose rock betrays their position to the gang.
The crooks force the kids into an old mine.
They leave them trapped to hunt for the treasure.
Suddenly, Captain Hadacol appears to save the day.
The mine entrance begins to cave in.
Rotten timbers seal everyone inside a living tomb.
The gang is finally turned over to the sheriff.
A big reward awaits for the captured crew.
The group realizes the treasure is still missing.

event.publisher: Creative Credit: Dudley "Coozan Dud" Joseph LeBlanc, Sr. (Youngsville, Louisiana, 16 August 1894 - 22 October 1971, Abbeville General Hospital, Abbeville, Louisiana)
event.description: Captain Hadacol, Comic Book Number 2 (Lafayette, Louisiana: LeBlanc Corporation, circa 1951). This comic book was issued as a promotional item for Hadacol, the tonic that Dudley "Coozan Dud" Joseph LeBlanc, Sr. (Youngsville, Louisiana, 16 August 1894 - 22 October 1971, Abbeville General Hospital, Abbeville, Louisiana) invented, manufactured, and sold as a kind of panacea for the aches and pains of adults and children. Although this booklet was issued as "Comic Book Number 2," it is not yet perfectly obvious, as of 2016, that a "Comic Book Number 1" of "Captain Hadacol" had ever been issued.
